metadata.description: Base name used as a prefix for resources. Lowercase letters and numbers work best.
Name of the resource group to create for all Photostore resources.
Azure region for the resource group and all resources.
Your login email. Used to sign in and to receive password-reset emails.
Your login password (at least 8 characters). You can change it later inside the app.
Where Azure Communication Services stores email data. Pick the option closest to you.

Where OCR/face/vision/geo processing runs. "browser" (default): entirely client-side, same as today -- no extra cost, works everywhere. "backend": the browser skips this work entirely and a new ipworker container processes every upload server-side instead -- better for low-power/mobile clients, and enables bulk background reprocessing of an existing library, at the cost of running ipworker (which needs meaningfully more CPU/memory than the rest of this deployment). "both": the browser and ipworker both attempt it and whichever finishes first for a given photo wins -- doubles compute cost per step, useful mainly for comparing the two paths.

Public backend image. Defaults to :latest for one-click "Deploy to Azure" installs. When upgrading an EXISTING deployment, override with the immutable date-time tag from the publish workflow run (e.g. :20260806-153045) instead of :latest, so scale-to-zero cold-start restarts keep pulling the exact image you tested rather than whatever :latest has drifted to.

Public frontend image. Defaults to :latest for one-click "Deploy to Azure" installs. When upgrading an EXISTING deployment, override with the immutable date-time tag from the publish workflow run instead of :latest, for the same reason as backendImage above.
Public ipworker image. Only pulled/deployed when processingMode is "backend" or "both". Same :latest-vs-pinned-tag guidance as backendImage applies when upgrading an existing deployment.
Base name used as a prefix for resources. Lowercase letters and numbers work best.
Azure region for all resources. Defaults to the resource group location.
Your login email. Used to sign in and to receive password-reset emails.
Your login password (at least 8 characters). You can change it later inside the app.
Where Azure Communication Services stores email data. Pick the option closest to you.

Where OCR/face/vision/geo processing runs. "browser" (default): entirely client-side, same as today -- no extra cost, works everywhere. "backend": the browser skips this work entirely and a new ipworker container processes every upload server-side instead -- better for low-power/mobile clients, and enables bulk background reprocessing of an existing library, at the cost of running ipworker (which needs meaningfully more CPU/memory than the rest of this deployment). "both": the browser and ipworker both attempt it and whichever finishes first for a given photo wins -- doubles compute cost per step, useful mainly for comparing the two paths.

Public backend image. Defaults to :latest for one-click "Deploy to Azure" installs. When upgrading an EXISTING deployment, override with the immutable date-time tag from the publish workflow run (e.g. :20260806-153045) instead of :latest, so scale-to-zero cold-start restarts keep pulling the exact image you tested rather than whatever :latest has drifted to.

Public frontend image. Defaults to :latest for one-click "Deploy to Azure" installs. When upgrading an EXISTING deployment, override with the immutable date-time tag from the publish workflow run instead of :latest, for the same reason as backendImage above.

Public ipworker image. Only pulled/deployed when processingMode is "backend" or "both". Separate from backendImage (unlike the clustering `worker` role, which reuses it) because ipworker needs torch/open_clip/onnxruntime/opencv/mediapipe/tesseract -- multiple GB of extra weight that would slow every backend/worker cold start if bundled into their shared image. Same :latest-vs-pinned-tag guidance as backendImage applies when upgrading an existing deployment.
Secret used to sign login sessions. Leave blank to auto-generate a strong random value at deploy time.
